heard: Male deep-sea anglerfish dissolve their own bodies to survive. In the pitch-black deep-sea, finding a mate is nearly impossible for the 200 known species of anglerfish. Females use bioluminescent lures to attract prey and can swallow animals twice their own size. Moving down the ladder, male photochorinous spinaseps are among the smallest vertebrates at about 7 millimeters long. That makes the massive female up to 60 times larger than her tiny mate. When a male finally finds a female, he latches on with his teeth to begin a permanent transformation. His eyes and internal organs slowly wither away until only his reproductive organs remain. He can fuse into her body because he lacks the immune genes that would normally reject foreign tissue. This dependence on her blood supply is why.
differences: 'photocorynus spiniceps' heard as 'photochorinous spinaseps' after 'the ladder male'
